title: `string` is text; binary data is a distinct `bytes` type
scope:
the `string` and `bytes` primitive types; the UTF-8 invariant on `string`; the conversion
between them; the default granularity of `string` length, indexing and iteration

summary.headline: Text and raw bytes are two different types
summary.body:
In PHP a string is both a piece of text and a buffer of bytes, and nothing tells you which one
you are holding — that ambiguity is why it needs two whole families of string functions and a
global setting to make either half work. Novis splits them. Text is always valid UTF-8 and
counts the characters a reader sees; raw data is its own type and counts bytes. Turning raw data
into text is checked, and it can fail.
